examples.text: Er is veel water door de muur gesijpeld.

glosses: langsam, in dünnen Rinnsalen, oder tropfenweise fließen

examples.text: Überschüssiges Wasser sickert in den Boden.

glosses: To ooze or pass slowly through pores or other small openings, and in overly small quantities; said of liquids, etc.

examples.text: Water has seeped through the roof.
The water steadily seeped in through the thirl.

glosses: To enter or penetrate slowly; to spread or diffuse.

examples.text: Woe seeped through her heart thinking of what had befallen their ethnic group.
Fear began to seep into the local community over the contamination of their fishpond.

glosses: To diminish or wane away slowly.

examples.text: The resistance movement against the invaders had slowly seeped away.

glosses: (of a crack etc.) To allow a liquid to pass through, to leak.

examples.text: If the crack is seeping water, the foam totally stops the leakage.
Just when I thought I was done checking it over, I smelled coolant....remove the engine cover and bam! 1 inch crack is seeping coolant!
wi' the weet / We're seepit to the skin
a young lad's mind, whilk had seeped in, for many a day, the rain of adversity

glosses: A small spring, pool, or other spot where liquid from the ground (e.g. water, petroleum or tar) has oozed to the surface; a place of seeping.
Moisture, liquid, gas, etc. that seeps out; a seepage.
The seeping away of a liquid, etc.

examples.text: Another idea was that filamentous bacteria covering the hairs [of the Yeti crab] would either neutralize gases emitted from the vent or serve the crab directly as a food source. And this last idea received support when a second species of Yeti crab was discovered on cold seeps on the deep-sea floor near Costa Rica.
